column1: # Shrink-only legacy record for the piped-`grep -q` idiom (#852).
# Format: <count><TAB><path>, highest count first. A comment cannot run, so
# comment lines here are not counted as occurrences.
# WHY these are recorded rather than fixed: `grep -q` exits on its first match,
# the producer is then killed by SIGPIPE, and `set -o pipefail` promotes that
# 141 to the status of the whole pipeline -- so a report larger than the 64 KiB
# pipe buffer reports ABSENT for text that is PRESENT. Negated that is a false
# red; positive the control is skipped and the check fails OPEN.
# Recording is an EXPLICIT REVIEWED ACT and is never automatic: a new occurrence
# is refused by name first. Fixing one is always welcome -- delete or lower its
# line and re-run with --record. Lowering the record is the only change that
# does not need a review of the code it describes.
# scripts/check-verdict-contains.sh records 3, and none of them is a verdict
# test: one is the provocation in section 1, which must exist for that control
# to be able to fail, and two are the planted fixture in section 3 -- one of
# which is the line that is SUPPOSED to read as a comment (it begins with a
# quote, so the counter sees it, which is the conservative direction).
# RECORDED WITH A DOCUMENTED REASON (#1838) -- three files whose NEW occurrences
# were read in context, measured, and judged a LEGITIMATE USE rather than the
# shape this check exists to prevent (a containment test piped into a quiet
# `grep`). None of the three is a containment test over the script's own report:
#   scripts/check-pr-contract.sh (17; was 15) -- the two new sites are NOT
#     containment tests. `grep -qE '[^[:space:]]'` (line 940) asks whether the
#     extracted section holds any non-whitespace character (a NON-EMPTY test),
#     and `grep -qE '^<the code-review-sme report'` (line 942) is a LINE-ANCHORED
#     prefix match; neither is expressible as the bash-native containment test
#     this check enforces. Measured: this file's only `set` line is `set -u`
#     (line 236) -- it does NOT set `pipefail`, so a SIGPIPE-killed `printf`
#     cannot be promoted to a 141 and cannot flip either verdict. The
#     pre-existing 15 remain the file's legacy verdict tests, untouched.
#   scripts/pr-body.sh (1) -- `printf '%s\n' "$labels" | grep -qx 'type:epic'`
#     (line 55) is a WHOLE-LINE EXACT match over the issue's `gh` label list. A
#     substring test (`contains`) would also match `type:epic-ish`, so grep's
#     line semantics ARE the requirement here, and the producer is one issue's
#     label list (bounded, small). Legitimate use, not a containment test.
#   scripts/prune-worktrees.sh (1) -- `printf '%s\n' "$manifest_jobs" | grep -q
#     '^MANIFEST-ERROR:'` (line 240) is a LINE-ANCHORED probe that detects the
#     manifest helper's error line; `contains` cannot express an anchored match.
#     The producer is the output of one `python3` probe over
#     config/fleet-jobs.json, bounded by the job count. Legitimate use.
# The fourth finding, scripts/run-lane.sh (2), WAS a genuine occurrence and was
# FIXED rather than recorded (#1838): a self-test verdict over the script's own
# captured output, both pure containment tests, in a file that sets `pipefail`
# (line 45) -- converted to the bash-native `contains` from lib/common.sh.
# measured: 2026-09-21 -- 113 site(s) in 50 file(s). This pass (#1838) raised
# scripts/check-pr-contract.sh 15 -> 17 and added scripts/pr-body.sh (1) and
# scripts/prune-worktrees.sh (1), each with the reason recorded above, and drove
# scripts/run-lane.sh 2 -> 0 by fixing it.
